evals.prompt: I want to move off Gmail to my own domain with a new email provider, and take 15 years of mail and my Google Drive files with me. How do I do this without losing anything or locking myself out?
evals.expected_output: Individual lane: back up first; migrate mail (imapsync/import) and files (rclone) with count/size checks; CRITICAL order — repoint recovery email + re-enrol 2FA on important accounts BEFORE closing Gmail; forward old address during grace; keep Gmail until verified, close last (one-way door); DNS/MX + SPF/DKIM/DMARC for the new domain. Points to individual-checklist.

assertions.name: backup_first
assertions.text: Says make and verify a backup before moving

assertions.name: recovery_before_close
assertions.text: Repoint recovery email / 2FA before closing the old account

assertions.name: verify_counts
assertions.text: Check message counts / file sizes rather than assuming it worked

assertions.name: close_last
assertions.text: Keep old account until verified; deleting is the last one-way step

evals.prompt: Our 60-person company is moving our on-prem file server, Exchange, and a line-of-business app with its SQL database to the cloud. What order, and how do we not break anything?
evals.expected_output: KMU lane: inventory + dependencies; a strategy per system (7 Rs — e.g. repurchase email, rehost files, replatform the DB); dependency-ordered waves (identity/DNS first, app after its DB); data migration with reconciliation; a cutover window per system with a tested rollback; keep source until reconciled. Suggests wave_planner.

assertions.name: dependency_order
assertions.text: Orders by dependency (DB before the app on it; identity/DNS early)

assertions.name: strategy_per_item
assertions.text: Assigns a strategy (7 Rs) per system rather than one blanket approach

assertions.name: rollback
assertions.text: Plans a rollback and keeps the source until verified

evals.prompt: Give me the migration strategy options — I keep hearing lift-and-shift, replatform, refactor and I don't know which to pick for our 200 apps.
evals.expected_output: Explains the 7 Rs (retire, retain, rehost=lift-and-shift, relocate, repurchase, replatform, refactor) with when each fits; stresses Retire/Retain (don't move dead weight), default to lowest-effort R, and avoid refactoring during the move. Frames it as tag-every-app-with-an-R portfolio assessment.

assertions.name: names_7rs
assertions.text: Covers the 7 Rs including retire and retain

assertions.name: refactor_caution
assertions.text: Warns against refactoring during the migration

evals.prompt: We have a big-bang cutover planned for our ERP this weekend. What should be in place before we flip the switch?
evals.expected_output: Verified backup; rehearsed runbook with owners/durations/critical path; final rehearsal timings fit the window; reconciliation checkpoint after load; go/no-go criteria with named evidence and one decision owner; rollback written and tested with a defined point of no return; comms; hypercare after. May suggest whether big-bang is even right vs phased/parallel.

assertions.name: tested_rollback
assertions.text: Requires a rollback written and tested before cutover, with a point of no return

assertions.name: go_no_go
assertions.text: Go/no-go criteria with named evidence and a single decision owner

assertions.name: rehearsed
assertions.text: Runbook rehearsed on a copy with real timings

assertions.name: reconciliation_checkpoint
assertions.text: Reconciliation checkpoint before opening to users
